en: A thousandfold I will worship you.
Tree of precious [?] fruit, fruit-bearing sapling,
Litter (carrier) of God, mother of God,
White bud [?] of the amancay lily,
Honoured one [?], what I have offered [?],
What I have hoped for [?], to your child
notes: General: colonial Quechua in Pérez Bocanegra's 1631 spelling; 'Dios' is the Spanish word for God. The hymn is addressed to the Virgin Mary. Several word divisions and suffixes are uncertain: read the [?] marks as real doubt. This translation should be checked by a reader of colonial Quechua.
line 1.1: 'Hanacpacha' (hanaq pacha) is the upper world, heaven; 'cussicuinin' its joy, gladness.
line 1.2: 'Huaran cacta' is read as waranqakta, 'by the thousand'; 'muchascaiqui' from much'ay, to kiss, revere, worship.

line 1.3: 'yupai' is esteem, honour (also 'count'), 'ruru' fruit, 'pucoc' ripening or bearing, 'mallqui' a young tree or sapling (also a revered ancestor). A Marian image of Mary bearing Christ as fruit; the division 'yupairuru / pucocmallqui' is the source's.
line 1.5: 'callpannac' is 'one without strength' (kallpa + -naq); 'quemicuinin' their prop, support.
line 1.6: 'Huaciascaita' is read as waqyasqayta, 'what I have called, my cry'; 'hear' is supplied from 2.1, as the verse ends here.
line 2.2: 'rampa' is a litter, a carried chair: Mary as the one who carried God.
line 2.3: 'tocto' is taken as a bud or sprout (uncertain); 'hamancai' is the amancay, an Andean lily; the ending '-man' ('to, towards') is hard to fit and may tie the line to what follows.
line 2.4: 'Yupascalla' is 'the esteemed, honoured one'; 'collpascaita' is unclear: 'what I have offered' is a guess.
lines 2.4-2.6 form one request: 'show to your child (Christ) what I have offered (?) and hoped for (?)'; 'suyuscaita' is taken from suyay, to wait, to hope.
